Matched RecHarness Amazon task: four datasets Movies_and_TV,
Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl, macro-average validation
HR@10. Start from RecHarness sasrec_perdataset. Preprocessing seed=0 and training
seed=42, exactly as run2.sh. The host executes your train.py and then independently
evaluates working/predict.py using the pinned RecHarness benchmark (200 validation
users/category, 99 unique negative candidates, evaluation seed=42). Test labels and
test metrics are unavailable during search. Retain all four categories and dataset
routing. DATA_DIR must remain os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write artifacts beneath
your trial directory, as the baseline does. Training may change model architecture,
loss, optimizer, sampling and hyperparameters, as in RecHarness. Do not alter input
splits, invent metrics, read hidden test files, fetch extra datasets/pretrained weights,
or change the host evaluator. Changes to inference must also update the predictor
writer so working/predict.py loads the trained architecture. Keep execution single-GPU;
the host provides four concurrent trial slots and 64 CPU cores. No shell actions,
filesystem inspection, or training tools are needed in the LLM call: return code.
All training, diagnostics, debugging and failed trials consume the method's shared
43,200 GPU-second search budget. LLM time and final held-out inference are recorded
separately, matching run2.sh's separate final-evaluation step.
The original RecHarness tools layer sets SASREC_EPOCHS=200 (overriding the template's
standalone default of 300); this same environment default applies here.

METHOD: self_evolverec

Diagnostic task adapter: diagnosis_tools.py must retain class DiagnosisProbe(view, device)
and method run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions.
view.model is the actual trained nn.Module. view.item_emb, log2feats(sequence),
predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, review_data implement the
initial SASRec compatibility contract. Adapt probes when changing the architecture.
train_loader yields (None, sequence, positive, negative), tensors of shape B x L.
Only public interaction histories, item titles, descriptions and timestamps are available.
Review ratings/text, item ratings/categories/prices/stores are NOT available in this
shared RecHarness task. Never invent them. Simulator diversity/conformity traits are
explicitly unobserved. Twenty real training users (five/category) receive full-catalog
unseen-item recommendations, as the native simulator requires. Selection uses the
common macro validation HR@10, replacing the native HR@5/NDCG@5 combined score.

NATIVE ROLE: Reflection Agent

You are an expert research assistant. You will receive a research report (in Markdown) and a newly proposed idea for that report's research problem. Your job is to identify any gaps or issues—such as missing details, logical flaws, or questionable evaluations of novelty, impact, or implementation difficulty.  

- If the report and idea contain all necessary information, do not generate any follow-up questions.  
- If you detect a knowledge gap or something that needs deeper exploration, generate one or more self-contained follow-up queries. Each query must include enough context so that a web search could answer it, For each query, give a short note explaining why you use the query and what you hope it will reveal.
- Focus on technical details, implementation specifics, and any emerging methods or references that were overlooked.  
- Use clear, direct language and avoid unnecessary jargon.

## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

The probes use the item embedding table (`item_emb.weight`), sequence encoder (`log2feats`), and scoring function (`predict_score`). Model implementation is absent, so the encoder architecture and final user representation cannot be verified. Diagnosis scores features at every sequence position; it does not explicitly extract a final user vector.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(model, device)` stores the supplied model or compatibility view, metadata, review data, and training histories. Only metadata is subsequently used. Under the adapter contract, these hooks come from the view, while `view.model` holds the trained module; evaluation mode must reach that module.

The margin probe calls `eval()` and disables gradients. It reads up to ten training batches containing `(None, sequence, positive, negative)`, each tensor shaped B × L. Sequences pass through `log2feats`; positive and negative IDs are stacked into B × L × 2 and scored together. Positions with positive ID zero are excluded.

# Probes & Metrics

- **Embedding collapse:** Sample up to 2,048 non-padding item embeddings with seed 42, normalize them, average off-diagonal cosine similarities, and map the result using `(cosine + 1) / 2`. Higher values indicate greater directional alignment; approximately 0.5 indicates mean cosine near zero, not necessarily collapse.
- **Positive–negative margins:** Compute positive score minus sampled-negative score. Report mean, lower tenth percentile, fraction below zero, and fraction below 0.5. Larger margins and smaller failure fractions generally indicate clearer separation.
- **Category breakdown:** Count categories associated with positive and negative items in weak-margin and wrong-ranking positions, retaining the twenty most frequent categories per group. These are raw counts, not normalized error rates.

# Perturbation & Tests

No sequence shuffling, masking, replacement, or sensitivity testing occurs. Random embedding sampling and existing training negatives provide the only sampled comparisons.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations

`run_full_diagnosis(train_loader)` returns `metrics` and `metric_definitions`, containing five scalar metrics plus a nested category breakdown. An optional interpreter prompt requests a separate JSON assessment with status, findings, implications, and evidence; it does not itself execute interpretation.

Category metadata is unavailable in this task, so category lists remain empty. Reviews and histories are unused. Probes do not measure validation HR@10, full-catalog ranking, sequence sensitivity, or simulator traits. Empty margin samples return zeros, which can misleadingly resemble healthy failure rates.


 ## Search results
Recent work supports history interventions as diagnostics of model dependence. [Measuring Recency Bias (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.09722) reports that excessive recency emphasis can impair recommendation accuracy. [Counterfactual Explanations via Genetic Algorithms (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.03606) searches for minimal sequence edits that change recommendations; fidelity measures agreement with model behavior, not correctness of inferred preferences. [Temporal Attribution Benchmark (2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.27201) evaluates explanations using a separately trained, masking-robust probe, explicitly examining popularity confounding and input corruption. Its experiments favor GradientSHAP and Integrated Gradients over raw attention as faithful attribution methods.

Practical synthesis: evaluate natural training-history prefixes; compare recent-window removal, older-window removal, suffix-only truncation, and order shuffling while holding item identities fixed. Test repeated-interest dependence using groups defined from observed interactions or title/description similarity, without claiming latent intent is observed. Replace selected interactions with items matched on training popularity and temporal availability; compare against equally sized random edits and popularity-only rankings. Track fixed-candidate rank shifts, top-10 overlap, and next-item accuracy separately, stratified by history length, recency, and popularity. These are proposed controls rather than a single established protocol. Large perturbation effects indicate model sensitivity; accuracy changes provide additional evidence about usefulness. Masking can create unfamiliar inputs, and observational edits alone cannot establish causal preferences or prove that recommendations are correct.

## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

The probes use the item embedding table (`item_emb.weight`), sequence encoder (`log2feats`), and scoring function (`predict_score`). Model implementation is absent, so the encoder architecture and final user representation cannot be verified. Diagnosis scores features at every sequence position; it does not explicitly extract a final user vector.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(model, device)` stores the supplied model or compatibility view, metadata, review data, and training histories. Only metadata is subsequently used. Under the adapter contract, these hooks come from the view, while `view.model` holds the trained module; evaluation mode must reach that module.

The margin probe calls `eval()` and disables gradients. It reads up to ten training batches containing `(None, sequence, positive, negative)`, each tensor shaped B × L. Sequences pass through `log2feats`; positive and negative IDs are stacked into B × L × 2 and scored together. Positions with positive ID zero are excluded.

# Probes & Metrics

- **Embedding collapse:** Sample up to 2,048 non-padding item embeddings with seed 42, normalize them, average off-diagonal cosine similarities, and map the result using `(cosine + 1) / 2`. Higher values indicate greater directional alignment; approximately 0.5 indicates mean cosine near zero, not necessarily collapse.
- **Positive–negative margins:** Compute positive score minus sampled-negative score. Report mean, lower tenth percentile, fraction below zero, and fraction below 0.5. Larger margins and smaller failure fractions generally indicate clearer separation.
- **Category breakdown:** Count categories associated with positive and negative items in weak-margin and wrong-ranking positions, retaining the twenty most frequent categories per group. These are raw counts, not normalized error rates.

# Perturbation & Tests

No sequence shuffling, masking, replacement, or sensitivity testing occurs. Random embedding sampling and existing training negatives provide the only sampled comparisons.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations

`run_full_diagnosis(train_loader)` returns `metrics` and `metric_definitions`, containing five scalar metrics plus a nested category breakdown. An optional interpreter prompt requests a separate JSON assessment with status, findings, implications, and evidence; it does not itself execute interpretation.

Category metadata is unavailable in this task, so category lists remain empty. Reviews and histories are unused. Probes do not measure validation HR@10, full-catalog ranking, sequence sensitivity, or simulator traits. Empty margin samples return zeros, which can misleadingly resemble healthy failure rates.
